label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=7), content-gated
explanation: Almost exclusively a delimiter-step unit: 91% of active steps and 93% of activation mass are at the <DEL> step (t == L), and it is essentially silent during the original phase (1% of mass) and the copy phase (6%, scattered weak activations, mostly on the first copy output). Firing rate rises steeply with sequence length: 0.1% of <DEL> steps at L=3-5, about 3% at L=6, 9% at L=7, 26% at L=8, 30% at L=9; L>=7 holds about 90% of the mass. Even at L=9 it fires on only about 30% of delimiter steps, and which ones depends on the stored content in a distributed, position-specific way: early-position tokens a/c/j (orig(0), orig(1)) and late-position tokens h/3 (orig(7), orig(8)) raise the rate to 50-60%, while e.g. s at position 0 or h at position 1 lower it below 10%. No single token being present or absent explains it, so this content gating is not captured by the predicate, which is why precision is low (about 0.22).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output, by phase (copy phase: c, v, a, y; delimiter step: j, v, i, a; input phase: ) and the third original token (most: q, s, w, y, a, 1; least: g, i, o, 2); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, L=8 & t=7, t=8.
